summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled shell and filesystem access on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs a long-running agent that connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches server-originated messages to handlers that (a) spawn an interactive PTY via pty.spawn($SHELL) in the agent's workDir and write inbound `terminal_input` bytes directly into the PTY, and (b) perform arbitrary filesystem operations on the host (`read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`) with server-supplied paths, streaming file contents back to the server. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint therefore obtains interactive shell execution and arbitrary file read/write/delete on the installer's host as the user running the agent, gated only by a shared `AGENT_SECRET`. A separate `upgrade_agent` message triggers `npm view` + `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the public npm registry and re-registers the service via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the connected server force installation of any currently-published version of the package. While the remote-control shell and filesystem access are the package's advertised purpose, they constitute a network-reachable backdoor and RCE surface on any host where the agent is deployed, and the security of every such host reduces to the secrecy of `AGENT_SECRET` and the trustworthiness of the configured server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
